skill.name: open-skills
skill.description: Interactive CLI for discovering, installing, syncing, and managing AI agent skills across multiple coding editors.
skill.summary: Manage AI agent skills for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and related editors from one CLI.
skill.author: lumacoder

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, TypeScript import paths, template literals, lockfile metadata, and Unicode text. Confirmed issues are limited to trust-sensitive external network lookups, developer-panel innerHTML rendering, remote skill installation into AI editor targets, and unauthenticated local registry mutation in dev mode. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Developer server allows unauthenticated registry writes with wildcard CORS.
remediation.suggestion: Bind the server to localhost explicitly, remove wildcard CORS, require a local nonce for POST routes, and reject requests from unknown origins.

remediation.issue: Remote skill content can be installed into AI editor configuration directories.
remediation.suggestion: Show source, commit or tag, and content diff before installation, and require confirmation for global installs or remote sources.

remediation.issue: Developer panel renders registry values with innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Render registry fields with textContent or escape HTML before insertion into the DOM.

remediation.issue: Create command accepts unvalidated positional skill names.
remediation.suggestion: Apply the same slug validation to positional arguments and reject paths containing separators or traversal segments.

remediation.issue: Directory installs may clean files in managed editor targets.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict cleanup to files marked by open-skills, show a deletion preview, and require explicit confirmation before removal.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Developer Registry Write API
semantic_findings.description: The developer server exposes state-changing registry APIs without authentication and allows all origins. If the server is reachable by untrusted browser content or network clients, registry data can be replaced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly shows dev-mode startup, wildcard CORS headers, and POST /api/registry writing parsed JSON. Exploitability depends on the dev server running and being reachable.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Skill Content Installed Into AI Editor Targets
semantic_findings.description: The install and sync flows clone registry-controlled git sources and write transformed skill text into AI editor skill or rule locations. This is expected behavior, but unreviewed remote skill text can influence assistant behavior after installation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation clones remote origins, reads SKILL.md content, transforms it, and writes it into editor targets. Malicious impact depends on registry content and user selection.

semantic_findings.title: Managed Directory Cleanup Before Install
semantic_findings.description: Directory-mode installs call cleanup on the computed editor target before generating output. This can remove files inside managed skill directories when users keep manual files there.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The engine calls cleanDirectory for directory adapters before writing outputs, and adapter code writes into computed target paths. The precise removal logic is in a helper not included in static findings, so confidence is moderate.

semantic_findings.title: Create Command Allows Positional Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: The interactive create flow validates prompted names, but a positional CLI name is accepted before path construction. A local user can pass traversal segments and create files outside the intended bundles directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code validates only the prompted name path and then joins the resulting name into bundles/skills. The issue requires local CLI input, which limits severity.

content.value_statement: AI coding teams often maintain separate skill files for each editor. open-skills provides one CLI to discover, install, sync, and manage shared skill content.
actual_capabilities: Starts an interactive CLI for choosing editors, install scope, categories, and skills.
Installs selected skills into Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo-Cline, Hermes, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot targets.
Lists, searches, validates, exports, and imports skill registry data.
Synchronizes selected GitHub or git-backed skills into local bundles with shallow clone and sparse checkout.
Provides a development panel for creating skill scaffolds and editing registry metadata.
Transforms skill content into editor-specific directory or rule-file formats.
limitations: Remote search and sync require network access and local git support.
Global installs write into editor configuration directories in the user home directory.
Directory-mode installs may clean unmanaged files inside managed target folders.
The development web panel is intended for local use only.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team AI Editors
use_cases.description: Install the same approved skills into several AI coding editors so contributors share consistent assistant behavior.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Skill Registry
use_cases.description: Create, validate, export, import, and synchronize a curated registry of reusable skills for internal workflows.

use_cases.title: Test Cross-Editor Output
use_cases.description: Generate editor-specific outputs for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf, and related tools from one skill source.

prompt_templates.title: Install Selected Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Use open-skills to install frontend and devops skills into Claude Code and Cursor for this workspace. Explain each prompt choice before proceeding.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the open-skills registry for skills related to testing and API design. Summarize the best matches and the editors they can target.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Local Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new local skill scaffold named api-review-checklist in the backend category. Explain which files were created and how to validate it.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Sync Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the registry for remote git or GitHub origins. Identify which skills can be synchronized, then run the safest sync plan for one selected skill.

output_examples.input: Install two frontend skills into Claude Code for the current project.
output: The assistant opens the editor, scope, category, and skill selection flow.
It writes selected skills under the Claude Code skills directory for the selected scope.
It reports which skills succeeded and which failed.

output_examples.input: Export my current AI skill setup.
output: The assistant detects installed directory-mode skills for supported editors.
It writes a stack file that can be imported later.
It explains any editor targets that cannot be detected automatically.

output_examples.input: Create and validate a new skill scaffold.
output: The assistant creates a local bundle with a starter skill file.
It registers the skill metadata in the registry.
It runs registry validation and reports any missing fields.

best_practices: Review remote skill content before installing it into global editor directories.
Use local scope first when testing new skills or registry changes.
Back up existing editor rule files and skill directories before install, update, sync, or import commands.
anti_patterns: Do not run the developer web panel on a shared or exposed network interface.
Do not install unreviewed remote skills directly into global AI editor directories.
Do not store personal files inside managed editor skill directories.

faq.question: What editors does open-skills support?
faq.answer: It targets Claude Code, Hermes, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Cursor Skills, Roo-Cline, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot.

faq.question: Does it download remote content?
faq.answer: Yes. Search, resolver, sync, and install paths can fetch GitHub, SkillStore, or git-backed skill sources.

faq.question: Can it overwrite existing editor files?
faq.answer: It refuses unmanaged rule files for some adapters, but directory installs clean files outside the expected managed set.

faq.question: Is the developer web panel for production use?
faq.answer: No. It is a local development tool and exposes unauthenticated registry APIs when started.

faq.question: Can it create new skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The create command and developer panel generate starter skill files and registry entries.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: The metadata marks Codex support, and the CLI can manage shared AI agent skill content for Codex workflows.
